answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post trades, with one stake permitting only a small amount of activity. A registry records the lock and penalizes proven fraud by slashing the stake, while honest agents can reclaim it after a delay. This does not make identities impossible to fake; it makes a swarm costly: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risk losing it. A glacier of cheap accounts melts against that price, whether their names are yarrow or sable.
